oewn-00497754-v.learner: To leave something as it is, without changing it.
examples: The soup tastes fine as it is, so just let it be.

oewn-00120604-v.learner: To make something move, or to put someone or something into a certain place or state.
examples: Agreeing to help him let me in for a long, hard week.

oewn-02213685-v.learner: To give someone the right to use or live in something under the terms of a contract.
examples: They let the cottage to a young couple for the summer.

oewn-05821331-n.learner: Any thing or person that you feel warm affection for or are devoted to.
examples: Music was always her great love.

oewn-00848145-n.learner: Sexual activity between two people, often including having sex.
examples: They made love for the first time that night.

connotation.why: frames sexual activity as warm and romantic, against plain 'sex'

oewn-13617812-n.learner: A score of zero in tennis or squash.
examples: She won the first game at love.

oewn-06297048-n.learner: A unit of language that people who grew up speaking it can recognize.
examples: And I am not so certain that I should myself use the word "narrow" in connection with her.

oewn-06750911-n.learner: A short thing that someone says.
examples: You know, sister, we agreed long ago never to mention a word about it.
you will find me as good as my word.

oewn-06654787-n.learner: News about important things that have happened recently.
examples: Word of the victory reached the town the next morning.

oewn-07155367-n.learner: A talk in which people share what they think about something.
examples: Could I have a word with you about the plan before the meeting?

oewn-07183893-n.learner: An order, given in words, to do something.
examples: Wait until I give the word, then run.

oewn-06686933-n.learner: A secret word or phrase that only the people in a certain group know.
examples: Only members who knew the word were let inside.

oewn-13648798-n.learner: A row of bits (0s and 1s) stored together in a computer's memory.
examples: Each word in this computer's memory is 64 bits long.

oewn-86559942-n.learner: A close male friend who goes along with his friends in the things they do.
examples: He's not family, but he's my brother; we go everywhere together.

connotation.why: claims family-like closeness and loyalty, against plain 'friend'

oewn-05857811-n.learner: A typical quality that seems to make something what it is and different from other things.
examples: The old harbour town has kept its quiet character.

oewn-09928518-n.learner: A person of a certain kind, usually one who is odd or unusual in many ways.
examples: Her uncle is a strange character who wears a top hat to the shops.

connotation.why: marks the person as odd or eccentric

oewn-06831828-n.learner: A written sign that stands for spoken language.
examples: Chinese is written with thousands of different characters.

oewn-05937794-n.learner: The part an actor plays, showing a person in a play.
examples: She played the character of the old queen with great warmth.

oewn-06707541-n.learner: A formal recommendation from someone's past employer to a possible new employer, describing the person's skills and how reliable they are.
examples: Her last employer gave her an excellent character.

oewn-04624273-n.learner: In genetics, a feature of a living thing, in its structure or in how it works, that is set by a gene or a group of genes.
examples: Eye colour is a character controlled by several genes.

oewn-05958593-n.learner: What most people believe or feel about something; what the public as a whole says.
examples: Opinion in the town was turning against the new mayor.

oewn-06563775-n.learner: The legal document in which a court sets out the reasons for its decision.
examples: The judge's written opinion ran to forty pages.

oewn-01193648-n.learner: The reasons a court gives for its judgment, as separate from the judgment itself.
examples: The court upheld the ban, but its opinion rested on privacy rather than free speech.

oewn-09410115-n.learner: The line or path along which something travels or moves.
examples: We followed the course of the river down to the sea.

oewn-03124441-n.learner: An area of land or water, with set limits, that is laid out for a sport.
examples: The golf course had only nine holes.

oewn-08698960-n.learner: The general direction that something takes.
examples: Past the hills, the river takes a southern course.

oewn-07572535-n.learner: One part of a meal that is served at one time.
examples: Soup was served as the first course.

oewn-08255384-n.learner: A group of students who are taught together.
examples: The whole course went on a trip to the museum.

oewn-03124680-n.learner: In building, one layer of bricks or stones.
examples: The builder laid another course of bricks on top.

oewn-01021031-s.learner: Having a body that is strong and healthy.
examples: After months of illness, he was finally fit and able again.

oewn-06753097-n.learner: Something that makes it right or fair for a thing to exist or happen.
examples: "I have no reason, I assure you," said he, "to be dissatisfied with my reception.

oewn-05659525-n.learner: The power to think clearly, to work things out from facts, or to tell things apart.
examples: Only humans, the old books said, were given the gift of reason.

oewn-14403234-n.learner: The state of having good sense and sound judgment.
examples: Please listen to reason and stay home tonight.

oewn-01237517-n.learner: A reaction to something that is not made in words.
examples: His only answer was to slam the door.

oewn-06572245-n.learner: The defendant's main formal reply to the complaint in a court case, which in a criminal case is a plea of guilty, not guilty or no contest, and in a civil case must deny each claim the defendant wants to fight and may add other defences or claims back against the other side.
examples: The company filed its answer, denying each claim in the complaint.
